newsitem.title: USA: Bayer gets FDA approval for diabetes tabs.
newsitem.headline: Bayer gets FDA approval for diabetes tabs.

text.p: Bayer AG's U.S. unit said on Thursday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted market clearance for its Glyset tablets diabetes treatment.
The drug is for treating Type II, or non-insulin-dependent, diabetes mellitus.

Glyset is the second alpha-glucosidase inhibitor developed by Bayer. Earlier this year, Bayer launched Precose tablets, the first alpha-glucosidase inhibitor for the treatment of Type II diabetes in the U.S.
Glyset and Precose slow down the digestion and absorption of ingested carbohydrates through the small intestine, Bayer said.

This decreases the exaggerated rise in blood glucose levels which occurs after meals in diabetic patients, and as a result, reduces levels of glycosylated hemoglobin, also known as hemoglobin Alc, which is an index of long-term blood glucose concentration, it added.
Two large studies undertaken by Bayer have shown that Glyset is particularly effective among Hispanic and African-American Type II patients, the company said.
It said Type II diabetes is more prevalent and is more commonly associated with complications in these subpopulations compared with Caucasian Type II patients.
